subject: Business
specVersion: Issue 2, February 2026 (as stated in the specification PDF text read); first teaching September 2017, first exam June 2019
statusNote: Replaces the earlier UK GCSE 1BS0 file. The correct qualification is Pearson Edexcel International GCSE Business 4BS1. Opened: the Pearson International GCSE Business (2027) landing page (a new qualification, teaching from September 2027, so not relevant to a 2026-28 cohort) and the 4BS1 specification PDF. The PDF was read through a page-summarising fetch tool, not page by page. Paper structure, marks, weights, assessment objectives, command words, quantitative skills, formulae and the section 1 to 5 topic titles with their headline content were obtained. Full bullet-level wording of every sub-topic was not read, so status is Provisional. Not opened: the Pearson 4BS1 qualification page for the current course, sample assessment materials, mark schemes. Year and term allocation is a recommended sequence, not a board requirement.

sources.title: Pearson Edexcel International GCSE (9-1) Business 4BS1 specification (PDF)
Pearson International GCSE Business (2027) page (new qualification; confirms last assessment of 4BS1 is November 2028)

years: Years 10 to 11 (linear two-year course, all assessment at the end)

assessment.title: Investigating small businesses
assessment.content: Whole specification, set in the context of a small business (up to 49 employees, local or national market)
assessment.format: Four compulsory 20-mark questions mixing multiple choice, short answer, data response and open-ended writing; calculator allowed; June and November series

assessment.title: Investigating large businesses
assessment.content: Whole specification, set in the context of a large business (more than 250 employees, multinational or global market)
assessment.format: Four compulsory 20-mark questions mixing multiple choice, short answer, data response and open-ended writing; calculator allowed; June and November series

nonExam: None: 100% external written papers. Quantitative skills are 10% of total marks across both papers, always in a business context. Six ratio formulae are provided in the exam. Assessments use International Accounting Standards terms (for example statement of financial position, inventory).

aos.desc: Recall, select and communicate knowledge and understanding of business terms, concepts and issues
Apply knowledge and understanding using terms, concepts, theories and calculations in context
Select, organise and interpret business information from sources to investigate and analyse issues
Evaluate business information to make reasoned judgements and reach conclusions

units.title: Business objectives
points: Financial aims include survival, profit, sales, market share and financial security
Non-financial aims include social objectives, personal satisfaction, challenge, independence and control
Objectives change with market conditions, technology, performance, legislation and internal reasons

units.title: Types of organisation
points: Sole traders, partnerships, private and public limited companies and public corporations
Compare forms by risk, ownership, limited liability, control, finance and use of profits
Stakeholders and shareholders; judging which ownership form suits a business
Franchises, social enterprises and multinationals

units.title: Classification of businesses
points: Primary sector businesses extract resources
Secondary sector businesses convert materials into goods
Tertiary sector businesses provide services

units.title: Location decisions
points: Location depends on proximity to market, labour, materials and competitors
The nature of the activity shapes the location choice
The internet allows e-commerce instead of fixed premises
Legal controls and trade blocs influence where a business locates

units.title: Market research
points: Research identifies customer needs and market gaps and reduces risk
Primary methods: surveys, questionnaires, focus groups, observation, test marketing
Secondary sources: internet, market reports, government reports
Qualitative and quantitative data, social media and reliability of results

units.title: The market
points: Marketing meets customer needs and builds relationships and loyalty
Market orientation versus product orientation; niche versus mass marketing
Businesses respond to changing needs, spending patterns and competition
Segmentation by location, demographics, lifestyle, income and age

units.title: Marketing mix
points: Product: new product development, goods versus services, packaging, life cycle, extension strategies, Boston matrix
Price: cost-plus, penetration, competition, skimming and promotional pricing
Place: retailers and e-tailers (e-commerce)
Promotion: advertising, sponsorship, trials, offers, branding, above and below the line, PR
Online promotion: targeted advertising, viral social media marketing and e-newsletters

units.title: Communication
points: Good communication matters to a business
Communication methods, including IT, have benefits and limitations
Barriers to communication and how to remove them

units.title: Recruitment and selection
points: Employment types: full-time, part-time, job share, casual, seasonal, temporary
Documents: job description, person specification, application form, CV
Internal versus external recruitment; advertising, shortlisting, interviewing
Legal controls: equal opportunities and minimum wage

units.title: Training
points: Training matters to the business and to workers
Induction, on-the-job and off-the-job training
Training supports health and safety compliance; benefits and limitations

units.title: Motivation and rewards
points: Motivation helps attract and retain staff and raises productivity
Theories of Herzberg, Maslow and Taylor
Financial methods: remuneration, bonus, commission, promotion, fringe benefits
Non-financial methods: job rotation, job enrichment, autonomy

units.title: Organisation structure and employees
points: Hierarchical versus flat structures; centralised versus decentralised decisions
Span of control, chain of command and delegation
Functional areas: human resources, finance, marketing and production

units.title: Sources of finance
points: Finance needs are short-term or long-term, for start-up or expansion
Internal sources: personal savings, retained profit, selling assets
External sources: overdrafts, trade payables, loans, share capital and flotation
Venture capital and crowdfunding

units.title: Cash flow forecasting
points: Cash pays suppliers, overheads and employees; shortages risk insolvency
Cash and profit are different things
Calculate and interpret inflows, outflows, net cash flow, opening and closing balances

units.title: Costs and break-even
points: Revenue, fixed costs, variable costs, total costs, profit and loss
Break-even output by formula or diagram
Interpret charts and the effect of changes in revenue and costs; know limitations

units.title: Financial documents
points: Statement of comprehensive income: sales, cost of sales, gross profit, expenses, operating profit
Statement of financial position: current and non-current assets and liabilities, capital employed
Candidates interpret these documents but do not construct them

units.title: Accounts analysis
points: Ratios: gross and operating profit margin, markup, ROCE, current ratio, acid test ratio
Judge liquidity and compare over time or with other businesses
Use financial documents to assess performance and inform decisions

units.title: Economies and diseconomies of scale
points: Internal and external economies of scale
Diseconomies and the limits of growth

units.title: Production, lean production and technology
points: Job, batch and flow production; labour- versus capital-intensive methods
Calculate productivity and the effect of improving it
Lean production: just-in-time, Kaizen and effective use of resources
Technology such as robotics: balancing cost, productivity, quality and flexibility

units.title: Factors of production
points: Enterprise, capital, land and labour as factors of production
How their relationships change; capital-intensive versus labour-intensive activity

units.title: Quality
points: Quality matters for goods and services
Quality control and total quality management (TQM)
Quality as a source of competitive advantage

units.title: Business and the international economy
points: Globalisation: concept, opportunities and threats
Multinationals: benefits to the firm, and benefits and drawbacks for host countries
Calculate exchange rate conversions
Exchange rate changes affect competitiveness, importers and exporters

units.title: Government objectives and policies
points: Government spending on public services; taxation and limits on spending
Infrastructure, legislation and trade policy such as trading blocs and tariffs
Interest rate changes affect businesses and consumer spending

units.title: External factors
points: Social, technological, environmental and political influences on business decisions

units.title: Business success
points: Success measures: revenue, market share, customer satisfaction, profit, growth, owner and employee satisfaction
Failure reasons: cash flow or lack of finance, uncompetitive, failure to adapt

commandWords.meaning: Select one or more correct answers; recall or a calculation
Give the meaning of a term from the specification
Give an answer that tests recall of specification knowledge
Give an answer of up to a sentence, chosen from the context
Select the correct answer from a graph or table
Apply maths to given data and show working
Work out the missing values in a table
Give two linked points about a concept, placed in context
Make a statement with two expansion points; no context needed
Extended answer exploring a concept in context
Extended answer using given information to recommend one of two options
Extended answer using knowledge to reach a supported conclusion

skills: Quantitative skills (10% of marks): percentages, percentage change, averages
Revenue, cost and profit calculations; gross and net profit margin; average rate of return
Cash flow forecast calculations and interpretation
Interpreting graphs, charts, profitability ratios and market data
Applying knowledge to small-business and large-business contexts
Extended writing: analyse, justify and evaluate with a reasoned conclusion
Reading and writing English at roughly CEFR B2 level; desk calculator allowed, battery or solar only

prerequisites.from: KS3 Mathematics: percentages, averages and substitution

links.topic: Percentages, percentage change, averages and ratio
links.how: Maths supplies the methods; Business applies them to margins, ROCE and liquidity ratios
Break-even by formula and diagram uses linear graphs and algebra from Maths
Exchange rate calculations use ratio and proportion

links.topic: Persuasive writing, audience and branding language
links.how: Promotion and branding rely on persuasive language; English develops analysis of purpose and audience
Analyse, justify and evaluate answers need reasoned, supported conclusions

links.topic: E-commerce, digital communication and online marketing
links.how: Computing explains the technology; Business assesses its effect on place and promotion
Spreadsheet skills support building cash flow forecasts and break-even tables
Geography covers where and why production locates; Business covers the firm's decisions and effects on host countries
Geography provides environmental evidence; Business weighs it against cost and profit

links.topic: Lawful trade, honest dealing and the rules on interest (riba)
links.how: Sources of finance such as loans can be discussed alongside Islamic teaching on trade, kept factual and separate from the exam content

links.topic: Fair treatment of workers and ethical conduct
links.how: Motivation and rewards can be compared with Islamic teaching on fair pay and conduct; enrichment, not examined
Arabic First Language topic 7 uses work and employment themes that recruitment content supports
Science underpins robotics and production technology; Business evaluates cost, productivity and quality

contextNote: Both papers use real-style business contexts (small business in Paper 1, large or multinational in Paper 2). Teach the range of business viewpoints accurately and let pupils evaluate. Islamic perspectives in the links are enrichment and are not examined.
gaps: Specification PDF read through a page-summarising fetch tool, not page by page. Bullet-level wording was not checked for every sub-topic, so points are paraphrased headline content only (notably 2.5 functional-area detail and 5.1 to 5.4).

Section and topic titles and numbering come from the fetch summary; confirm against the PDF contents page. The fetch listed three items numbered 5.2 (production, lean production, technology) and these are merged into one unit 5.2 here.
4BS1 Paper 1 and Paper 2 test the whole specification; no board allocation of sections to papers exists, so every unit lists Papers 1 and 2.
Assessment objective weightings recorded as ranges as the specification states them; per-paper approximate percentages not recorded.

The spec header showed Issue 2, February 2026; confirm the current issue and series dates with Pearson. The 2027 landing page states the last assessment of 4BS1 is November 2028, so a cohort starting Year 10 in 2026 sits within the window.
Sample assessment materials, mark schemes, examiner reports and the Pearson 4BS1 qualification page were not opened.
The school's lesson files were written to UK GCSE 1BS0 unit titles and do not match 4BS1; they need re-mapping.
Whether the school enters for 4BS1 (not UK GCSE 1BS0) should still be confirmed with the exams officer; the brief states International GCSE.
